knowledge:
- key_parameters: subject=A DNAString object representing the input sequence to search ;; min_score=Minimal score of PQS to be reported (default is 52, which shows the best balanced accuracy on human G4 sequencing data) ;; overlapping=Logical; if TRUE, overlapping PQS will be reported instead of only the locally best non-overlapping PQS ;; deep=Logical; if TRUE, enables calculation of overlapping PQS numbers at each position, allowing the use of density() ;; max_defects=Maximum number of defects in total (bulges + mismatches) allowed in G-runs (range 0 to 3) ;; custom_scoring_fn=A user-defined function to customize or completely replace the default scoring system ;; use_default_scoring=Logical; set to FALSE to completely disable the default scoring system (e.g., when searching for alternative structures like interstrand G4s) ;; run_re=Regular expression defining a run of the quadruplex (used when customizing/replacing default scoring)
- alternatives: triplex=A Bioconductor package mentioned for users who want to search for triplexes (another type of non-B DNA structure) instead of G-quadruplexes
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to identify potential G-quadruplex forming sequences (PQS) in genomic or transcriptomic sequences, especially when you want to allow for imperfect G-runs containing bulges or mismatches, or when you want to model custom G4-like structures.
- pitfalls: In each G-run, the algorithm allows at most one type of defect, and at least one G-run must be perfect (without any defect). Consequently, the values of max_bulges, max_mismatches, and max_defects must fall strictly within the range from 0 to 3. Custom scoring functions can negatively influence overall algorithm performance, particularly on long sequences. If use_default_scoring is enabled, the custom scoring function is evaluated after the DSS but only if the DSS resulted in a positive score.

workflows.name: g4_detection_and_export
workflows.intent: Detect potential G-quadruplexes in a DNA sequence, analyze their density, and export the results to GFF3 or FASTA formats.
input: sequence.fa (FASTA file containing the DNA sequence of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Load sequence into a DNAString object ;; 2. Run pqsfinder to detect potential G-quadruplexes ;; 3. Extract metadata and calculate density ;; 4. Convert results to GRanges and export to GFF3 ;; 5. Convert results to DNAStringSet and export to FASTA
workflows.code:
library(pqsfinder)
seq <- DNAString("TTTTGGGCGGGAGGAGTGGAGTTTTTAACCCCAAAAATTTGGGAGGGTGGGTGGGAGAA")
pqs <- pqsfinder(seq, min_score = 20)
pqs
elementMetadata(pqs)
pqsfinder(seq, overlapping = TRUE, min_score = 30)
pqs <- pqsfinder(seq, deep = TRUE, min_score = 20)
density(pqs)
gr <- as(pqs, "GRanges")
gr
library(rtracklayer)
export(gr, "test.gff", version = "3")
dss <- as(pqs, "DNAStringSet")
dss
writeXStringSet(dss, file = "test.fa", format = "fasta")

workflows.name: custom_g4_detection
workflows.intent: Detect non-standard or customized G-quadruplex structures (such as interstrand G-quadruplexes) using custom scoring functions and regular expressions.
input: sequence.fa (FASTA file containing the DNA sequence of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Define a custom scoring function ;; 2. Run pqsfinder with the custom scoring function ;; 3. Define an alternative scoring function and regular expression for complete replacement of the default scoring system ;; 4. Run pqsfinder with default scoring disabled
